notes.1: This question was answered well by most candidates. Candidates of lower ability generally obtained credit for only four of the six available marking points, giving a partially complete answer for the thickness of the block as 4.4 cm.
notes.3: This question was well answered by most candidates.
notes.4: The first three parts of this question were answered well by candidates of all abilities. All except the least well-prepared candidates were able to explain the actions needed to make the thermometer give a zero reading.
notes.5: This question was answered well by better prepared candidates. A small but significant number of candidates, however, did not make responses to various parts of this question indicating gaps in their knowledge and understanding. Unfortunately there were some very poorly presented ray diagrams. Candidates need to be encouraged to draw neat diagrams using thin, single lines that have been drawn with the aid of a ruler. Candidates should not expect to be given credit for inaccurate or poorly presented ray diagrams. Part (c) was answered correctly by only a small number of candidates.
notes.6: This question was answered well by the large majority of candidates.
notes.7: This question was answered well by candidates of all abilities.
notes.8: This question was answered well by those candidates that had revised this section of the syllabus carefully. A number of candidates did not make responses to parts (c) and (d) .
notes.9: This question proved to be challenging for candidates of all abilities. A significant number of candidates failed to make responses to various parts of this question indicating that their knowledge and understanding was not secure. Very few correct responses were seen to part (c) (ii) .
notes.10: This question was not answered well by candidates. Again a significant number of candidates did not make responses to some parts of this question, for example parts (b)(i) and (c)(i) .
notes.11: This question was answered well by only the best prepared candidates. Again a significant number of candidates did not make responses to some parts of this question including parts (a)(i) , (a)(ii) and (a)(iii) , also part (b)(iii) .
notes.12: Those candidates who had not revised the transformer equation were unable to calculate the output voltage from the transformer. A number of candidates did not attempt the calculation or the last part of this question.
notes.2a: This question proved challenging for candidates of all abilities. Kinetic energy was a common incorrect response, with candidates not taking note of the statement: “They run up the hill at a steady speed”.
notes.2b: This was correctly answered by only the best prepared candidates.
notes.2c: A common misconception was to give an answer related to the athletes’ preparation and fitness.
